title: Mercy Is Rejected and Anti-Sikh Proclamations Begin

blocks.text: The deputation's appeal fails completely. Lakhpat Rai is denounced for the killing of Bhai Mani Singh, yet he refuses even a short delay for Somvati Amavas and treats every request for mercy as proof that the Khalsa's enemies must press harder, not relent.

His rage spreads beyond executions into symbolic persecution. The Guru's hymns and sacred texts were concealed, the public utterance of Waheguru was suppressed, and even the name of the Guru became something officials tried to erase from open life.

Having rejected both mediation and religious restraint, the state now moves openly toward war. Lakhpat Rai uses proclamation and sacrilege together, preparing artillery, troops, and orders for a campaign that will hunt the Singhs far beyond the towns where the arrests began.
